notes: Base Avantis (dual-screen, 64x42) model. Rear panel and Technical Specifications drawn directly from the official Allen & Heath "Avantis Getting Started Guide" (AP11558 Issue 5, support.allen-heath.com), which lists a numbered rear-panel diagram (12 items) and front-panel diagram (2 items). Mic/Line Inputs are combo-style XLR sockets accepting balanced/unbalanced mic or line signals (documented as "Balanced XLR" in the Technical Specifications; treated here as XLR3 since no separate 1/4" TRS combo barrel is called out, though many A&H consoles use XLR/TRS combo jacks — noted as a minor uncertainty). Digital Inputs/Outputs are stereo AES3 pairs, each physically an XLR3 connector carrying 2-channel AES3 (not RCA/BNC AES); labeled here as "AES3 In" / "AES3 Out" using xlr3 connector since that is the documented physical connector (AES3 is a protocol/grade context, not in the given grade enum, so grade omitted per instructions — AES3 is not one of the gradable connector types listed). The 2 "I/O Ports" are 128x128 expansion slots that accept optional cards (Dante, MADI, gigaACE, AES, DX Link, Waves SoundGrid, etc.) rather than fixed physical connectors themselves; they are not included as individual ports since their physical connector varies by installed card (uncertain/variable — see notes). SLink port is a locking Neutrik etherCON (RJ45-form-factor) carrying Allen & Heath's proprietary SLink protocol for remote I/O expanders (GX/DX/AB/AR ranges) and ME personal monitoring — mapped to connector "ethercon"; no grade applied since SLink is a proprietary protocol, not standard Ethernet, and the source does not state an IEEE speed. Network ports are standard Gigabit Ethernet (RJ45) for Avantis Editor/iOS app control — grade eth-1g per "2 RJ45 Gigabit Ethernet ports." USB rear socket is USB 2.0 (Type-A, per Getting Started Guide); front sockets are USB 3.0 (Type-A) plus 1/4" (TRS 6.35mm) and 1/8" (TRS 3.5mm) headphone jacks. Word Clock I/O is a single BNC connector (bidirectional per device documentation: "BNC connector for syncing from an external audio clock or providing a clock to other devices. In and Out LEDs indicate current mode") — modeled as one bidirectional BNC port; no SDI-style grade applies since word clock is not video/data. Desktop/console form factor — no rackUnits (mixing console chassis, not rack-mount). Power: single IEC C14 inlet, 100-240V AC 50/60Hz, 150W max. Variants exist (Avantis Solo single-screen, Avantis Ultra) with different I/O counts — this entry is for the standard dual-screen Avantis console (64 channels/42 buses/12 XLR in/12 XLR out) as documented in the AP11558 Issue 5 guide.
